Recent advances have demonstrated the effectiveness of self-evolving LLM agents on tasks such as program
repair and scientific discovery. In this paradigm, a planner LLM continuously synthesizes agent programs that
invoke parametric components, including generative models such as LLMs, and fine-tunes them. However,
existing work has shown that self-evolving agent frameworks can exhibit undesirable behavior on unseen
inputs. Because these synthesized programs are often executed autonomously, the lack of formal guarantees
that hold for all inputs raises serious reliability and security concerns. To address this gap, we introduce
specification-driven self-evolving agent synthesis, which combines formal behavioral specifications that the
synthesized agents must satisfy on all inputs with best-effort soft objectives that capture task utility. We
propose Formally Guarded Generative Models (FGGM), which allow the planner LLM to bind each generative-
model call to a formal output contract. Each FGGM call automatically wraps the underlying parametric
generative model within a stateful rejection sampler and a verified fallback, treating model outputs as samples
from a proposal distribution. Consequently, every returned output satisfies the specified contract for any input
and any parameter setting of the underlying model. Building on FGGM, we present SEVerA (Self-Evolving
VerifiedAgents), a four-stage framework for specification-driven agent synthesis. In theIdeationstage, the

finding a specification-compliant program alone insufficient. Instead, the optimal solution requires
searching over all specification-compliant candidates and picking the one with the highest reward.
SEVerA systematically breaks down the search procedure into four tractable high-level steps,
combining the benefits of both constraint-guided program search from deductive synthesis and
unconstrained gradient-based parameter optimization. The first,Ideation, step extracts a fixed
number of task-specific generative componentsG using models fromF𝑝, thereby expanding the
setF𝑐. TheSearchandVerifysteps then perform deductive component-based synthesis to produce
parametric programs overG∪F 𝑐 that satisfy the specification(Φ,Ψ) over all parameter values.
Finally, the gradient-based optimization step fine-tunes the parametric models to jointly maximize
cumulative reward while complying with the formal contracts defined in the corresponding FGGM.
The proposed Formally Guarded Generative Model (FGGM) serves as the critical link between
these stages. During the ideation step, it binds each unreliable GM call to explicit local contracts

and a verified non-parametric fallback program, ensuring that these contracts hold regardless
of the underlying GM parameters. The synthesis step then leverages these local contracts to
prove the correctness of the parametric program with respect to the behavioral specification.
Beyond providing correctness guarantees, these contracts also extract local learning objectives by
characterizing the expected outputs of each GM call. This enables the final optimization step to
improve each GM’s conformance to its local contracts, connecting constrained program search
with unconstrained learning. Next, we discuss the key steps of SEVerA using two representative
and easy-to-understand problem instances from scientific discovery and program verification.
